correctness.rationale: Moradi's construction places tau_infty and gamma in the weak-star closure of traces of finite-dimensional representations; separability makes the same diagonal argument used in Lemma 3.1 show both are quasidiagonal. Theorem 4.1 forces every quasidiagonal trace to annihilate h=e^1-e^0, while the constructed chord has value c(2t-1) on this norm-one unitary, giving the lower distance bound. The quasidiagonal midpoint attains it because ||mu_1-mu_0||=2. Faithfulness follows from the positive gamma coefficient and amenability from faciality.

originality.rationale: The inspected arXiv:2609.18793v1 states an asymmetric non-face decomposition and the equal-sector-mass obstruction, but not the faithful symmetric midpoint family or exact norm-distance profile. Exact and synonymous searches around quasidiagonal traces, midpoint decompositions, norm distance, faithful non-quasidiagonal traces, and trace-simplex geometry did not locate this refinement. Standard convex-geometric and amenable-trace ingredients are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The refinement shows that failure of the quasidiagonal-trace face property is quantitatively robust in norm and persists with all relevant traces faithful and amenable: every prescribed distance c in (0,1) occurs at endpoints of a faithful chord whose unique quasidiagonal point is its midpoint.
